items.text: According to a FINRA arbitration award reported by InvestmentNews, Morgan Stanley sought to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans (along with attorney's fees and interest) from former advisor Sam Te Su; the advisor had already paid back the loans before the hearing.
items.quote: a sole FINRA arbitrator turned aside Morgan Stanley's attempt to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, along with attorney's fees and interest.

items.text: InvestmentNews reported that Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from former advisor Darryl Cohen via promissory notes (loans that brokers pay back to firms over time), and a FINRA arbitrator awarded Morgan Stanley $8.13 million in damages plus $561,000 in legal fees.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley sued Cohen in 2021 in a dispute over promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time. Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from Cohen.

items.text: InvestmentNews reported that Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan for advisors and is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027 (a different, retention-oriented compensation mechanism rather than recruiting compensation or forgivable loans).
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach. As it has in the past, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027
